### Actor, Interface, Storage, And Timing

```lisp
(actor apb_requester
  (clock clk)
  (reset (rst_n async active_low))
  (watchdog 65535)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (input req_addr (width 32))
    (output done)
    (output PADDR (width 32)))
  (storage
    (var captured_addr (width 32))))
```

This is the ordinary single-clock shape. For multi-clock actors, use
`(clock-domains ...)` instead of mixing it with `(clock ...)`:

```lisp
(clock-domains
  (domain bus  (clock bus_clk) (reset bus_rst_n))
  (domain core (clock clk)     (reset rst_n) :default))
```

### Acknowledged Event CDC

```lisp
(crossings
  (event rx_done
    (from bus  rx_done_req)
    (to   core rx_done_pulse)
    (ready rx_done_ready)))
```

The source domain may request only while `rx_done_ready` is true. The
destination domain receives a pulse later, after the generated CDC child moves
the event safely across the domain boundary.

`isf/clock_domain_no_reset_event_crossing.isf` covers the acknowledged-event
schedule/report surface when both domains omit resets. The generated CDC
metadata records `SOURCE_RESET_PRESENT 0d0` and `DEST_RESET_PRESENT 0d0`, and
the HDL path emits clock-only domain modules plus a generated CDC child without
absent reset ports.

### Transaction Body

```lisp
(transaction apb_transfer
  (on start
    (sample req_addr as addr))
  (set PADDR addr)
  (drive setup)
  (await PREADY)
  (complete done)
  (latency (min 2) (max 16)))
```

The scheduled `.fsm` review artifact owns the exact cycle placement: samples
materialize at the accepted entry boundary, drive calls consume states, awaits
test the selected port, and completion pulses the authored done output.

### Transaction Ports And Bindings

```lisp
(transaction read_word
  (ports
    (input addr (width 32))
    (output data (width 32)))
  ...)

(do read_word
  (bind
    (input addr req_addr)
    (output data read_data)))

(rule launch_read ready
  (trigger read_word
    (bind
      (input addr (+ base_addr offset)))))
```

Input bindings accept scalar signals, numeric literals, exact-width literals,
and non-empty list expressions. `do` and `spawn` support input and output
bindings; rule `trigger` supports input bindings only. Successful schedule
reports expose bounded `transaction_port_bindings[]` entries rather than raw
binding internals, with `actor_endpoint_kind` classifying the authored actor
side as `signal`, `literal`, or `expression` and `binding_timing` classifying
the transfer timing as `activation_region`, `generated_live_handoff`,
`trigger_payload`, or `done_guarded`. `authored_timing_mode` reports
`snapshot`, `live`, or JSON null for no explicit timing clause.

### Stage And Bounded-Eventually Monitor

```lisp
(transaction stream_word
  (on start)
  (stage wait_ready
    (ready ready)
    (valid valid))
  (assert (monitor (within done 8)) "finish_seen")
  (complete done))
```

The shipped stage surface is a top-level ready/valid barrier. The shipped
bounded-eventually surface is the `(assert (monitor (within SIGNAL N)) ["NAME"])`
monitor, which replaced the former top-level `(contract …)` clause. The older
`(input ready)`/`(output valid)` stage spelling remains accepted as an alias,
and the valid endpoint still participates in same-target conflict checks.
Monitor windows may use positive literals, declared positive actor constants,
actor-local scalar parameter defaults, qualified imported package scalar
constants, or same-transaction scalar parameter defaults on generated child or
direct/non-generated transactions when those sources resolve to positive
integers. Direct transaction parameters are local lowering inputs for this
monitor-window value domain and are not emitted as actor-level `.fsm`
`+params`.

Broader stage-local compute, nested stages, registered-valid/skid-buffer
variants, runtime-signal or expression monitor windows, min/max windows, and
global implication forms remain backlog.

### Waits And Repeat Bodies

```lisp
(params
  (WAIT_PARAM 2))

(transaction pulse_train
  (on start)
  (repeat count
    (drive pulse 1)
    (wait WAIT_PARAM)
    (drive pulse 0)
    (update count_seen (+ count_seen 1)))
  (complete done))
```

The repeat body may use the shipped inline body clauses documented in
[Transactions](13b-transactions.md) and [Control Flow](13d-control-flow.md).

`WAIT_PARAM` is an actor parameter wait count: scalar actor parameter defaults
that resolve to non-negative integer literals lower through the same static
wait contract as literals and actor constants. Same-transaction scalar
parameter defaults use that same static wait contract in their owning
transaction and shadow actor-level static names. Qualified package scalar
constants such as `shared.WAIT_PARAM` are accepted by that same static wait
contract when they resolve to non-negative integer literals.

A plain local `(do child)` and a same-domain generated `(do child (params ...))`
(with `(bind ...)`/`(domain NAME)` when static params are present) inside a
`(repeat ...)` that sits directly in a single `(while ...)` or `(until ...)`
body, plus the same plain-local and same-domain-generated `do` at deeper branch
nesting (`when⁺ → repeat`, `switch → when⁺ → repeat`), are part of the shipped
repeat-body subset. The first loop-plus-branch repeat-body activation is also
shipped for plain local `while -> when -> repeat -> do`; generated `do`,
spawn, `until -> when`, nested `switch`, and extra loop nesting in that family
remain deferred. The basic loop-contained/deeper-nested `spawn` + same-body
drain subset and multi-pending `await_any` with a later same-body `await_all`
drain are also shipped at lowering + composition-planning level. Deeper-nested
cross-domain repeat-body `do`, cross-domain `spawn`, undrained spawn forms,
repeats reached through an additional loop ancestor, and nested `stage` or
`contract` clauses remain outside the shipped repeat-body subset. Cross-domain
generated `do`, loop-contained/deeper-nested undrained `spawn`, and
extra-loop-ancestor repeat-body `do` each emit targeted diagnostics so authors
can identify which deferred lane is
blocking their specific case; the original generic "supported only for
top-level..." message remains as a safety-net fallback.

<details>
<summary>Repeat-body construction-rule audit markers</summary>

These short markers let the feature-matrix audit detect the shipped
repeat-body activation families without restoring the old exhaustive list of
individual spelling combinations:

```text
top-level repeat-body local blocking do
samples before or after spawn before same-body sync
samples before or after repeat-body do before the repeat check
multi-pending repeat-body await_any with mandatory same-body await_all drain
documented top-level when/switch nested-repeat activation construction rule
local do, generated-child do, static params, bind handoffs, same-domain metadata
await_any observation-only plus same-body await_all exact drain
```

</details>

### Types, Enums, And Aggregate Leaves

```lisp
(types
  (type mode_bits (bits 2))
  (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (valid bit))))
(enums
  (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
(storage
  (var frame (type frame_t)))

(transaction publish
  (on start)
  (set frame.mode mode.BUSY)
  (when frame.valid
    (set out_mode frame.mode)))
```

The shipped aggregate path is scalar-leaf based. `frame.mode` and
`frame.valid` are accepted because `frame` is declared actor-owned aggregate
storage and the paths resolve to scalar leaves.

Runtime expression divisor safety is fail-closed for literal zero, fixed actor
constants that resolve to zero, actor scalar parameters whose defaults resolve
to zero, and same-transaction scalar parameters whose defaults resolve to
zero:

```lisp
(constants (ZERO 0) (DEN 2))
(params (ZERO_P 0) (DEN_P 2))
;; inside a transaction: (params (TX_ZERO 0) (TX_DEN 2))
(set out (/ numerator divisor))  ;; accepted: dynamic divisor, no proof yet
(set out (/ numerator 8'd2))     ;; accepted: nonzero literal divisor
(set out (/ numerator DEN))      ;; accepted: nonzero actor constant divisor
(set out (/ numerator DEN_P))    ;; accepted: nonzero actor parameter divisor
(set out (/ numerator TX_DEN))   ;; accepted when TX_DEN is a nonzero same-transaction parameter
(set out (/ numerator 0))        ;; rejected before scheduled .fsm emission
(set out (/ numerator ZERO))     ;; rejected before scheduled .fsm emission
(set out (/ numerator ZERO_P))   ;; rejected before scheduled .fsm emission
(set out (/ numerator TX_ZERO))  ;; rejected when TX_ZERO resolves to zero
```

### Bank Store And Load

```lisp
(storage
  (bank data (width 8) (depth 4))
  (var wr_ptr (width 2))
  (var rd_ptr (width 2)))

(transaction fifo_step
  (on push)
  (store data wr_ptr data_in)
  (load data rd_ptr as data_out)
  (complete done))
```

The bank is scalarized in scheduled `.fsm` review text. Pointer-selected
access remains explicit through `store` and `load`; memory-array backend
emission is not a current support claim.

### Rules, Priority, And Resources

```lisp
(rule high write_req
  (set valid 1))

(rule low read_req
  (priority over high)
  (set valid 0))

(resources
  (resource rule_exec
    (kind rule_slot)
    (arbiter priority)
    (users high low)))
```

The shipped `rule_slot`/`priority`, `output_bundle`/`priority`,
`transaction_start`/`priority`, `storage_port`/`priority`, bounded
`rule_slot`/`round_robin`, bounded `output_bundle`/`round_robin`, bounded
`transaction_start`/`round_robin`, and bounded
`storage_port`/`round_robin` subsets can gate a whole bound rule DT for
one active cycle. Remaining resource kinds are documented names, not supported
runtime arbitration behavior yet.

### Generated Children

```lisp
(transaction worker
  (params
    (WIDTH 8))
  ...)

(transaction parent
  (on start)
  (spawn worker as w0
    (params
      (WIDTH 16)))
  (await_all done)
  (complete done))
```

The lowerer emits a scheduled parent `.fsm`, scheduled child `.fsm`, and a
generated top `.fsm`. The generated top applies static parameter overrides and
wires start/done handoffs.

### Reusable Library Use

```lisp
(imports
  (library common.fifo as fifo_lib))

(use fifo_lib.fifo as u_fifo
  (params
    (DATA_WIDTH 8)
    (DEPTH 4)
    (PTR_WIDTH 2)
    (OCC_WIDTH 3))
  (bind
    (clock clk)
    (reset rst_n)
    (input write_req write_req)
    (input data_in data_in)
    (output full full)
    (output data_out data_out)))
```

The cataloged `common.fifo.fifo` actor is a shipped reusable ISF library
definition. Library imports are semantic roots that still lower to scheduled
`.fsm`; they are not textual includes.

### Schedule JSON And Manifest Discovery

```bash
./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json isf/apb_requester.isf
./bin/fsmgen --capability-manifest
./bin/fsmgen --emit-capability-manifest
```

The schedule report is the machine-readable companion to the scheduled `.fsm`
review artifact. The capability manifest advertises the live ISF public
contract, including this book chapter through `live_document_paths`.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "actor_params": [
    { "name": "WIDTH", "value": 8 }
  ],
  "actor_phases": [
    { "name": "capture", "body": [["note", "metadata"]] }
  ],
  "actor_stages": [],
  "verification_observations": [
    {
      "name": "link_rx",
      "role": "passive_monitor",
      "clock": "clk",
      "reset": { "name": "rst_n", "kind": "async", "polarity": "active_low" },
      "signals": [
        { "name": "valid", "direction": "input", "width": 1 },
        { "name": "ready", "direction": "output", "width": 1 },
        { "name": "data", "direction": "input", "width": 8 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "inferred_storage": [
    {
      "name": "wait_count",
      "kind": "counter",
      "role": "dynamic_wait_counter",
      "width": 4
    },
    {
      "name": "done_fail",
      "kind": "register",
      "role": "temporal_contract_monitor"
    },
    {
      "name": "worker_process_start",
      "kind": "register",
      "role": "atl_trigger_start_handoff"
    },
    {
      "name": "last_error",
      "kind": "register",
      "role": "scheduler_error_status",
      "width": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

The manifest flag `schedule_report_full_schema_stable` is true for
`schema_version: 1`. Consumers should still prefer advertised keys, value
families, and explicit role fields over parsing generated signal names as
semantic API.

### Downstream Issue Bundles

```bash
./bin/fsmgen-issue-bundle \
  --case path/to/fsmgen-facing-artifact \
  --issue-id sf-0001 \
  --speforge-version "SPECFORGE_COMMIT" \
  --failure-class unknown \
  --expected "FSMGen should accept this generated artifact" \
  --observed "FSMGen rejects it" \
  -- --strict --check --json
```

Downstream tools do not need to decide whether the root cause is `.fsm`,
`.isf`, parser, lowering, HDL, or API-specific before filing. The bundle
captures the FSMGen-facing artifact, exact command, environment, observed
stdout/stderr/status, JSON probes, generated artifacts, and a rerunnable
`commands.sh` so the issue can be reproduced from the FSMGen repository root.

## Explicit Non-Claims

These are important because they prevent the matrix from implying support that
does not exist:

- Multi-bit CDC payloads, FIFO CDC, reset-as-event semantics, and direct
  cross-domain data access are not shipped.
- A cross-domain `(do CHILD)` directly inside any TOP-LEVEL body — a `(repeat ...)`
  body or a `when`/`switch`/`while`/`until` branch body — and directly inside a
  `(repeat ...)` nested in a top-level `when` body or top-level `switch` branch,
  plus directly inside supported nested `when` chains reached from those top-level
  branch bodies and repeats under those chains, IS shipped (the dual-CDC handshake
  runs when the branch is taken and re-runs each iteration inside a repeat/loop; see
  the cross-domain activation crossing row).
  Generated or spawned nested activation beyond the documented top-level
  branch-contained generated do
  cases and top-level branch-contained spawned cases, broader outstanding-child
  semantics, deeper branch repeat activation beyond the shipped top-level
  `when`/`switch` branch-contained repeat crossing, nested
  nested switch, repeat-contained branch, nested `while`, nested `until`, `stage`,
  `contract`, and DEEPER-nested cross-domain
  activation (a cross-domain `(do)` whose container is itself nested inside another
  body rather than a direct transaction-body clause) remain outside the
  shipped repeat-body subset.
- Dynamic division/modulo nonzero proof is not shipped. Literal-zero,
  actor-constant-zero, actor-parameter-zero, and
  same-transaction-parameter-zero divisors are rejected, but arbitrary runtime
  scalar divisors and nonzero use-site-specialized parameter divisors are
  emitted unchanged.
- Enum members are not writable targets, and enum members in expression
  operator position fail closed.
- Record output member writes, root-list interface ports, transaction-local aggregate
  ports, aggregate banks, subaggregate updates, and whole-record/list truthiness
  remain backlog. Whole record outputs/copies have bounded source/carrier admission
  above; packed record actor inputs have the qualified bounded admission above;
  this does not complete broader generated/domain/native or consumer delivery.
- Backlog resource kinds are registry names, not runtime arbitration support.
- Actor-level phase and stage metadata is report-only; it does not schedule
  actor-level runtime phases, barriers, generated `.fsm` states, or HDL
  behavior.
- Actor-level passive observation metadata is report-only; it does not emit
  generated `.fsm`, HDL, UVM, VHDL, scoreboard, coverage, or VIP artifacts.
  The shipped form is `(observe NAME (role passive_monitor) (signals SIG...))`
  over unique public actor interface signals in a single-clock actor.
- ATL generated-child actor-to-actor routes do not support generated-handoff
  remapping or reuse. Parent-declared collisions with selected trigger,
  event, data, or named-drive request handoff names fail closed with focused
  parser-owned coverage for normal `.isf` source and lowerer-owned coverage
  for malformed or mutated scheduler-facing actor metadata. This is not a new
  source feature. Route mux/storage, fan-in/fan-out, CDC/reset remapping,
  ready/backpressure, payload protocols, route drive parameters, route
  drive-call actual arguments, recursive actor networks, and permanent actor
  grouping also remain outside the shipped generated-child actor-to-actor
  route subset.
- Direct `(on ...)` activation-site `(params ...)` is unsupported and fails
  with an entry-guard/generated-activation diagnostic; static specialization
  belongs to spawn, generated blocking `do`, and rule-trigger generated
  activation sites.
- Rule-trigger output bindings for direct/local targets, explicit
  behavior-changing snapshot-vs-live binding timing selection/conversion,
  additional future binding-report expansions beyond the shipped bounded
  `transaction_port_bindings[]` summary fields, and broader static binding
  conflict diagnostics are not shipped. The shipped summary fields include
  `actor_signal`, `actor_expression`, endpoint kind, binding timing, and
  authored timing mode. The direct/local rule-trigger output-binding
  diagnostic names the missing generated-child completion identity. Duplicate
  output actor targets inside one bind block, and duplicate generated
  rule-trigger output actor targets inside one rule, fail closed before
  broader assignment conflict handling.
- Nested stages, stage-local compute/action bodies, multiple ready/valid
  endpoints, registered-valid variants, and skid buffers are not shipped.
- Temporal contracts beyond the top-level bounded eventual subset, including
  runtime-signal or expression windows, global implication forms, dynamic
  bounds, expression operands, and multiple outstanding obligations, are not
  shipped.
- Raw parser actor hashes, private `LoweringIR` internals, raw assignment
  provenance lists, and recursive child report dumps are not public schedule
  JSON API.
- VHDL is recognized as a target family, but the full VHDL backend is not
  shipped.

When a future slice widens any row above, update the detailed chapter, this
matrix, the live spec, the downstream handoff, the public contract or manifest
metadata when applicable, focused tests, and the feature backlog in the same
task-scoped commit.

# 0113 — ISF record interface ports reuse packed type and writer contracts

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Type: ISF language, lowering and public report contract
- Status: bounded input/output authoring admitted; complete output/consumer qualification remain open
- Owner: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.4.2`

## Context

The preserved SPECFORGE request is `docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/packet.json`.
Its required R1–R3 ask for declared packed record inputs/outputs, scalar field access, whole
same-type port/storage copies, and visible type/layout metadata. R4 list-root ports and R5 variant
records are optional. The intake's current refusals are historical evidence, not a new regression
oracle after delivery.

At selection, the parser admitted aggregate aliases only on storage variables. Lowering already
preserves interface type references in `+size`; core `.fsm` type/path machinery owns packed
representation. Generated internal storage handoffs do not establish authored aggregate-port
support. Decisions `0107` and `0109` retain state ownership, physical writer admission and execution
qualification. R13/R14 require stable public reports and ordered IAL1 → IAL0 lowering; this feature
must not add a second type system or bypass IAL0.

## Decision

### Source and value contract

Select `(input NAME (type T))` and `(output NAME (type T))` for an existing actor-local or imported
package-qualified alias resolving to a packed record. Reuse the existing recursive record/list
member type system, including nested members. Root list ports remain R4. Unknown types, malformed
declarations, unresolved/nonpacked types and unsupported carriers fail before successful lowering,
with the port/type/context identified. Width/type exclusivity, closed options, declaration presence
and existing domain ownership remain. Typed output reset/default options remain outside this request
and retain their current explicit refusal.

Input fields are live scalar reads in each already-supported scalar expression context: transaction
conditions, set/update RHS, rules and named drives. Existing explicit sampling remains the way to
request a snapshot. Resolve paths against the declared root type; unknown members, non-scalar leaves
and out-of-range nested items fail contextually. Do not infer fields by punctuation or admit
whole-record truthiness, arithmetic or subaggregate writes.

Whole copies involving a record port require the same resolved record type: compare recursive kind,
member names/order and scalar width/signed/state-model properties under the existing type resolver;
equal packed width alone is insufficient. Alias spelling may differ when it resolves to that same
type. Support input-to-storage and storage-to-output, then other port/storage directions whose
declared input/output roles permit the read/write. Inputs cannot become assignment targets. Preserve
existing storage-only packed transfers and scalar-port behavior; the new check applies to
record-port copies, not retroactively to all aggregate storage assignments.

Reuse typed `+size` and explicit `+interface` carrier entries. Record member order is authored
order, first member most significant, as already implemented by
`AggregatePathSupport::record_member_low_offset`. Scalar paths retain their leaf widths and exact
packed ranges. No scalarized public field pins, payload register copies, implicit reset, added
pipeline edge or silent arbitration.

### Detached public metadata

Select optional `source.interface_ports` on successful directly parsed ISF check/semantic reports,
and `interface_ports` in schedule JSON. One producer must project fresh JSON-safe values from parsed
declared ports through native, API and actual newline MCP; it must not export parser/private IR
objects. Unrelated source formats and failure reports gain no invented ISF declarations. Unknown
declaration metadata in caller-created actors remains null, rather than reconstructed from inferred
hardware signals.

The snapshot orders inputs in their authored order followed by outputs in their authored order,
matching the existing parser handoff. Entries contain `name`, `direction`, `width`, and optional
authored `type` and resolved `type_kind`; named-domain entries also contain `domain`. A record adds
`fields`, an ordered array of scalar leaves with port-relative `path`, `width`, `lsb`, `msb`,
`signed`, and optional `state_model`. Nested paths follow the existing aggregate path syntax. The
normalized semantic type catalog remains the authority for recursive type declarations. Schedule
domain details carry the same snapshot for their declared ports. Generated private handoffs do not
appear as authored top ports. Advertise every added field family in the public capability contracts
and qualify detached values and complete report parity.

### Delivery and qualification order

1. Implement the detached metadata producer on the currently admitted scalar
   interface, with record-layout producer controls. Prove unchanged scheduled
   FSM and HDL; this preparatory slice does not admit record source ports.
2. Admit and qualify packed record inputs, scalar reads and input-to-storage
   whole copies. Cover local/imported/nested types, invalid paths/types, unused
   declarations, domains and generated children under their existing bounds.
3. Admit output records and whole copies only with sound physical writer
   ownership/admission, preserving unrelated scalar and storage controls.
4. Add scalar output-field writes after qualifying physical packed-range
   overlap. Whole-root/member overlap and generated competing writers must
   refuse unless a demonstrated compatibility/exclusion contract admits them.
5. Qualify affected backend profiles and the complete supplied consumer
   outcome. Direct SystemVerilog/Verilog and supported VHDL subsets have
   separate obligations; an unsupported profile must refuse precisely.

Input delivery does not depend on general independent-controller repairs. Output writes consume
those prerequisites only where their actual behavior needs them. Native HDL observations require
existing HIAL admission and failure-only observation; never replay a spent capture to seek
recurrence. Each implementation leaf may split further before source changes.

## Consequences at selection

R1–R3 remain unshipped until their owned slices and consumer qualification pass. R4/R5 stay
separately owned optional follow-ups after required duration/timer work; transaction-local aggregate
ports, banks and variant syntax are not implicitly admitted. The book keeps present support
boundaries and labels this selection as future work. No external corpus counts, timing guarantees,
runtime signoff or downstream integration completion follow from this decision.

Permanent qualification must include independently authored packed values, member-order/type
mismatch and input-write negatives, unchanged baseline controls, complete native/API/newline
products, supported corpus cases, capability/spec/book alignment and recoverable downstream response
evidence.

## Producer implementation evidence — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.1` qualifies the detached producer independently of source admission and report
wiring. T1983 retains independently expected nested/imported ranges, signed/state-model leaves,
mutation isolation and invalid metadata. The draft's hostile controls found an argument-context
defect: a failed regex returns an empty list in list context, while an array returns its members.
Either can change the predicate/message argument slots of a validation helper. Predicates now return
explicit booleans or scalar counts; the helper also requires exact argument arity. This is a
producer repair, not a claim about uninspected validators or a public record-port implementation.

Reproduce the failed-regex mechanism independently:

```bash
perl -e 'sub predicate { $_[0] =~ /\A[01]\z/ } sub guard { print "arguments=",scalar(@_)," first=",($_[0] // "undef"),"\n" } guard(predicate(2), "error message"); guard(scalar(predicate(2)), "error message");'
```

The first call places the message in the predicate slot; the scalar call keeps both slots. The
permanent hostile controls verify refusal rather than accepting report parity as proof of valid
metadata. No native HDL runtime is established.

## Declaration report integration — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.2` captures validated parser declarations before scheduler port injection. Ordinary
module IR carries a fresh closed snapshot; domain sources select their original owned entries.
Generated transaction children have unknown declaration metadata, rather than pretending private
ports are actor declarations. Reports distinguish known empty arrays from unknown null; unrelated
and failed source reports omit the ISF source field.

The shipped preparatory surfaces are success `source.interface_ports`, schedule `interface_ports`
and owned `clock_domains[].interface_ports`, with one complete shared discovery descriptor at
`source_optional_fields.interface_ports` and `schedule_report_interface_ports`. T1984 independently
expects local/imported scalar declarations, unused/undriven entries, source order and domain
ownership; actual event crossings and generated children demonstrate private-port exclusion. This
report delivery does not admit authored records. Complete transport and supported-corpus
qualification remains explicitly owned by `.60.4.3.1.3` before record input implementation. No
native HDL runtime is claimed.

## Complete metadata qualification — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.3` qualifies complete typed native/API/actual newline products against independent
declaration witnesses. T1985 joins the live `build_source_query_cohort()` selector's ISF rows to
explicit reviewed source identities and declared port lists, then executes every applicable check,
semantic and schedule query. The selector owns supported catalog applicability; this is not a census
of product features, all repository fixtures or runtime coverage.
`feature.isf_declared_interface_metadata` now names this delivered metadata through the dedicated
`isf/interface_port_metadata.isf` fixture in the existing supported ISF pipeline corpus.

Local/imported aliases, unused/undriven declarations, known empty interfaces, a named empty domain,
malformed record/list/width refusals and unrelated FSM/PPIF reports receive complete transport
comparisons. Discovery compares complete native, in-process, API and newline sections. Canonical
typed JSON comparisons retain scalar kinds; shared field loss, wrong width/direction/order, private
data and stringified widths still fail independent expectations even when all three fabricated
transport copies agree. No parser or report values are repaired by the oracle. Source bytes remain
unchanged across queries.

Together with T1983/T1984 and the retained historical report/carrier/HDL controls, this closes the
preparatory declaration metadata lane. Authored record source ports and their hardware behavior
remain owned by the subsequent input/output leaves; no native HDL execution or complete consumer
delivery is established.

The corpus accounting control rejects duplicate `(relpath, classification, coverage)` tuples even
under different IDs. Reusing an existing source for the new identical contract failed that gate, so
the delivered metadata owns a separate runnable fixture. T248 also exposed stale exact expectations
from the prior storage-word-access entry (Git `3fa482924`, found with `git log -S`). The pre-slice
`241fad6b5` public catalog already exceeded those expectations; the new fixture adds only its
distinct entry. T248's exact census, tuple/ID and classification/strict checks and T1883's complete
cohort join retain the repair. Counts describe catalog entries, not independently implemented
features or runtime qualification. Recount from the live public catalog; do not reuse the old dated
qualification receipt as a current total.

## Record-input ingress selection — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.1` traces the refused input boundary before widening it. Parser
`_finalize_actor_type_references` admits aggregate aliases only on storage;
`_validate_actor_aggregate_storage_paths`, rule operand maps and enum disambiguation currently
select storage roots. Adding inputs to one map is insufficient. Use a shared declaration-root
description, with transaction locals/formals and drive parameters masking outer names in their
actual scope. An input shadowed by a writable formal must not become that formal's role; an
unresolved local must not borrow its outer type or placeholder width. The existing formal resolver
and domain ownership remain authoritative.

Prepare a strict resolved-record identity gate separately from
`PayloadTypeSupport::payload_compatible_with_type_spec`. That public helper intentionally checks
payload shape and scalar width, allowing different signed and state-model facts. Preserve it for its
existing callers. Port copies compare recursive kinds, ordered record members, ordered list
children, widths, signed values and optional resolved state-model presence/value. Unspecified stays
unspecified; do not substitute a backend rendering default. Alias names are not part of resolved
identity. Malformed/unresolved roots fail contextually.

Transaction conditions, switch values, set/update RHS, rule guards/assignments, named-drive
bodies/actuals and inline drives need explicit scalar-versus-copy checks from the first admission.
Whole-record values are permitted only in qualified same-type assignments with allowed declaration
roles; expression operators, truthiness and subaggregate writes refuse. Existing storage-only packed
transfers retain their separate contract. Domain lookup resolves a path to its declared root,
honoring lexical masking and preserving the authored path in diagnostics; it must not invent a
crossing from a same-named formal.

The current aggregate validator handles `set`, but not `update` or `sample` leaf paths. Sampling
width collection copies exact root widths, not resolved leaf facts. Input delivery therefore owns
explicit scalar-leaf sampling in entry/body contexts, with resolved width/type and existing capture
timing. Whole-record sampling into an inferred alias remains outside this bounded delivery. No
hidden sample, delayed edge or new aggregate local is introduced. Typed `+size` and explicit
`+interface` already preserve unused declarations; generated/domain routes must retain those
identities before behavior signoff.

Reproduce the historical identity/refusal control at pre-admission revision
`0d01ca3fc8f880acf926ae59305843a1172bf1d3`, without HDL:

```bash
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- perl -Iperl -MFSM::Adapter::ISF -MFSM::Package::PayloadTypeSupport -MJSON::PP -e '
my $p = FSM::Adapter::ISF->new;
my $a = $p->parse_source(q{(actor controls
  (types (type plain (record (payload (bits 8)))) (type alias plain)
    (type signed_frame (record (payload (signed (bits 8)))))
    (type four (record (payload (four_state (bits 8)))))
    (type two (record (payload (two_state (bits 8))))))
  (interface (output done))
  (storage (var a (type plain)) (var b (type alias))
    (var c (type signed_frame)) (var d (type four)) (var e (type two)))
  (transaction main (complete done)))}, "controls.isf");
my @t = map { $_->{type_spec} } @{$a->{storage}};
my $j = JSON::PP->new->canonical;
die "alias mismatch" unless $j->encode($t[0]) eq $j->encode($t[1]);
for my $pair ([0,2], [0,3], [3,4]) {
  die "control lost" unless $j->encode($t[$pair->[0]]) ne $j->encode($t[$pair->[1]])
    && FSM::Package::PayloadTypeSupport->payload_compatible_with_type_spec(@t[@$pair]);
}
my $ok = eval { $p->parse_source(q{(actor refused
  (types (type frame (record (payload (bits 8)))))
  (interface (input packet (type frame)) (output done))
  (storage (var held (type frame)))
  (transaction main (set held packet) (complete done)))}, "refused.isf"); 1 };
die "refusal lost: $@" if $ok || $@ !~ /interface port.*references aggregate type/;
print "alias identity, distinct property controls and input refusal verified\n";
'
```

The input lane now separately owns closed gates, source admission, generated/ domain carriers and
independent HDL/public completion. This planning receipt does not establish new input acceptance,
sampling support or native behavior.

## Unwired value-gate qualification — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.2` prepares `ISFRecordPortValues` without parser or scheduler wiring.
`record_value_scope` takes closed resolved outer/local declarations; the nearest binding masks its
outer type and role even when unresolved. `record_value_reference` retains scalar path
type/width/range through `AggregatePathSupport`, refuses input writes and whole/subaggregate scalar
values, and returns unknown tokens to their existing validator. The caller must still validate those
tokens and supply actual lexical bindings; a prepared map does not establish parser, domain or
generated-child integration.

`validate_record_port_copy` uses the existing composition declared-type comparison after closed
resolved-shape validation by the qualified declaration producer. Root aliases are absent from that
identity. Equal packed widths, renamed/reordered members, bit/bits kinds, nested shape/list order,
signed and optional state-model differences are independently distinguished. Transfers with no whole
record port keep their existing scalar/storage assignment owner. Scalar formal/local slices use a
one-member wrapper for existing core traversal; the wrapper preserves offsets and adds no source
carrier or type declaration.

T1986's draft negative helper matched an expected regex passed as a caller argument inside
`Carp::confess` stack text. That concealed a wrong-key diagnostic projection (`reason` instead of
the resolver's `code`), yielding `unresolved` for otherwise specific invalid paths. Restricting the

uninspected diagnostic oracles.

T1986 retains resolved alias/imported positives, independently authored ranges, same-width
counterexamples, lexical unresolved/scalar/formal shadows, input-role negatives, malformed/cyclic
facts, storage-only bypass and unchanged aggregate source refusal. T1983/T1259 and core path,

## Contextual integration and domain prerequisite — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.1` splits actual lexical/contextual gate preparation, explicit leaf sampling
carriers, declared-domain protection, first input admission and frontend/public replay before
implementation. Parser type finalization precedes aggregate/enum checks, but their current maps
select storage roots. Locals, formals, drive parameters and explicit samples require their actual
binding facts; inferred writes must not redefine an actor input. Sampling preparation must retain
signed/state facts as well as leaf width through existing typed carriers, with no new snapshot edge
or whole-record inferred local.

At pre-repair revision `02827d840254d6cdbfa4020be7910bb7ae9ac4cb`, public parse/lower probes reject
a foreign-domain whole scalar input and unsliced record-storage member, yet accept the same input's
bit/indexed slices and the member/storage scalar slices. `_validate_domain_signal_access` recognizes
only single-index path suffixes and only actor-storage roots for non-identifiers. The missing colon
form and interface-root exclusion bypass domain admission. This proves a source/lowering validation
defect; no HDL runtime is established. P1 repair `.60.4.3.2.3.4.1` is next, before unrelated
contextual implementation; `.4.2` retains future record/formal/domain qualification. Do not widen

Reproduce the bounded existing source defect without native HDL execution:

```bash
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- perl -Iperl -MFSM::Adapter::ISF -MFSM::Scheduler::ISF -MJSON::PP -e '
my $header = q{(actor domain_probe
 (clock-domains (domain core (clock clk) :default) (domain aux (clock aux_clk)))
 (types (type frame (record (payload (bits 8)))))
 (interface (input start) (input data (width 8) (domain aux)) (output seen (width 8)))
 (storage (var record_value (type frame) (domain aux)) (var scalar (width 8) (domain aux)))};
my @rows;
for my $token (qw(record_value.payload record_value.payload[3:0] scalar[3:0] data data[3:0] data[0])) {
 my $ok = eval {
  my $a = FSM::Adapter::ISF->new->parse_source($header
    . "(transaction main (on start) (set seen $token)))", "domain-probe.isf");
  FSM::Scheduler::ISF->new->lower($a); 1;
 };
 my ($message) = split /\n/, $@;
 push @rows, {token => $token, accepted => $ok ? JSON::PP::true : JSON::PP::false,
   diagnostic => $message // ""};
}
print JSON::PP->new->canonical->pretty->encode(\@rows);
```

## Actual declaration-scope preparation — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.2.1` prepares detached actor, transaction and drive scopes in
`ISFRecordPortScopes`. Actor ports and `var` storage consume finalized declaration widths and
resolved type facts. Transaction formals replace outer declarations; explicit top-level local
clauses provide the nearest width-only binding. Resolved type facts retain signed and optional
state-model properties. An unresolved typed declaration never uses its placeholder width. Symbolic

Named-drive parameters carry names without resolved types. They mask outer roles and types without
inferring a type from a drive target. Assignment targets create no declarations here. Explicit
sample aliases and their leaf facts remain owned by `.3.3`; contextual AST and enum/rule namespace
integration remain under `.3.2.2` and `.3.2.3`. These helpers are unwired, and record authoring
still refuses.

T1987 independently expects parsed symbolic/scalar/formal facts and imported record identity, exact
packed leaf ranges, signed/state properties, unresolved shadows, known input roles and mutation
isolation. Malformed declared widths, duplicate port roles and invalid parameter names fail.
Complete parsed actors and scheduled objects, including emitted file bytes, remain unchanged after
projection. The first draft fixture incorrectly assumed an authored pin/storage collision was
accepted; the actual parser refused it. The corrected fixture retains that refusal and the existing

their projection establishes no new source admission or physical identity contract.

Reverify with guarded T1987/T1986/T1983/T1259/T1391. The competing borrowed-type, placeholder-width
and inferred-target interpretations fail the independent scope/range witnesses and negative

Contextual preparation and first-touch caller-data correction are retained in

baseline followed an earlier projection; fresh copied facts now have independent pre-projection

Current record/formal domain preparation, repaired inline/named-drive ingress and the owned
unused-drive carrier defect are canonical in
[0114](../../0114-record-value-validation-detaches-facts-before-reading.md#recordformal-path-domain-preparation--2026-09-30).
The earlier domain receipts above retain their original capture boundaries.

## Parser/module gate integration — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.5.1` integrates prepared validation before `.5.2` admits record-input source
syntax. Parser resolved-type phases and shared formal/ executable module preparation now apply the
contextual scalar/copy/role/sample gate whenever actual record-input facts exist. Existing
storage-only path grammar remains with its original validator. Record-bearing enum exclusions use
the canonical nearest actor/transaction/drive projection; rule operands use its declared actor roots
and resolved aggregate roots. Ordinary scalar/ storage actors retain existing projections. This is
integration, not admission.

T1997 supplies finalized record facts at the real parser type-finalization boundary without
replacing production validators. Actual later phases retain layout metadata, scalar/formal/parameter
masks and enum namespaces, while refusing invalid members, input writes, wrong copies, whole scalar
values, operator references and unsupported contexts. Missing ordinary rule operands still reach
their original validator. Actual formal/executable boundaries have independent first-line negatives
and complete caller-JSON isolation controls.

Re-derive with guarded T1997 and the owning leaf's preparation/public cohorts. At immutable
predecessor `6f7b30bb4498f3ab13f294fae6a209342a4ef4c4`, the full pre-integration controls fail
parser namespace and module admission witnesses. Falsification also replaces only the shared
LoweringIR contextual gate call with an omission in an isolated repository-local include tree.
Preload that copy and run T1997: its module-admission subtest fails while parser phases and public
record refusal pass. Durability is these tracked producers, T1997 and this control recipe. Initial
draft fixtures were corrected to parenthesized drive formals and nonfatal diagnostic capture,
without product changes. Authored record ports still refuse; native/backend/consumer signoff remains

## Authored record-input admission — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.5.2` admits only resolved record-kind actor inputs through `.5.1`'s integrated
gates. Local/imported aliases must resolve to positive-width packed records. Root-list inputs,
record outputs, transaction aggregates and banks remain closed; unknown types and width/type
conflicts retain their owners. The scalar/copy/role/namespace/domain/sample contracts above remain
mandatory. Nearest scalar formals/drive parameters mask outer layouts; private samples retain leaf

snapshots reuse core carriers without new public keys, field pins or implicit sampling/reset edges.

At immutable predecessor `0d01ca3fc8f880acf926ae59305843a1172bf1d3`, T1998's actual local/imported
inputs fail resolved interface admission. Its maintained controls independently expect complete
nested layouts/type identities, unchanged caller JSON, schedule metadata and native
original-source/every-carrier strict success. Whole copies, scalar members/items/slices, control
reads, explicit samples, rules, drives, unused inputs and explicitly bound generated outputs pass.
First-cause type/path/role/context and foreign-domain negatives, including same-width wrong
recursive types, retain the selected boundaries.

The draft widened a five-bit leaf into an eight-bit output; strict native checking refused implicit
widening. Width-aligned outputs correct that fixture. An unbound generated child similarly refused
`job.seen`; record and ordinary scalar controls preserve that published contract. The corrected
positive declares a scalar formal and uses `(bind (output result seen))`. The subaggregate oracle
now expects the actual scalar-leaf diagnostic. These correct fixtures, not product defects.

Re-derive with guarded T1998/T1985 and the owning leaf's corpus/regression commands. Falsification
uses literal ordered layouts, equal-width type and input-write/scalar/context counterexamples,
pre-admission RED, catalog omission and native record/scalar unbound-child controls. Tracked

Complete generated/domain, native HDL, affected backend and supplied consumer qualification remain
owned by `.2.4-.2.5`; runtime is explicitly missing here and requires the HIAL failure-only

# 0114 — Record value validation detaches facts before reading

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Status: qualified context/sample/domain preparation; authored input admission follows 0113
- Owner: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.4.3.2.3.2.2`
- Parent contract: [0113](../../0113-isf-record-interface-ports-reuse-packed-type-and-writer-contracts.md)

## Context

Record inputs need contextual scalar reads and strict same-type copies before
their first authored source admission. Existing qualified value gates accept
resolved declaration facts, and detached scope preparation consumes parsed
actor/formal/local declarations and untyped drive parameters. This preparation
is still unwired; current scalar/storage authoring remains unchanged.

T1988's complete actor comparison exposed a mutation missed by the earlier
T1987 baseline: validation changed string widths into JSON numbers on fresh
copies of parsed facts. The earlier mutation baseline followed a previous
projection. Direct fresh parser controls stayed equal; the fresh copied
controls were RED. T1986 independently reproduced the same change in each
scope, reference and copy gate using explicitly string-valued widths.

## Decision

Detach caller-owned declaration/type/reference maps before numeric validation
or comparison. Perl numeric reads can change a scalar's flags and subsequent
JSON representation without an assignment to that scalar. A clone made after
validation cannot protect the original. `Storable::dclone` detaches before
reads and retains cycles for the existing closed type validator to reject;
core type/path/layout contracts remain unchanged.

Reproduce the mechanism independently:

```bash
perl -MJSON::PP -e 'my $j=JSON::PP->new->canonical; my $x={width=>"7"}; print $j->encode($x),"\n"; my $n=0+$x->{width}; print $j->encode($x),"\n";'
```

The outputs are `{"width":"7"}` then `{"width":7}`. This is a caller-data
mutation mechanism, not a new numeric value or public field contract.

`ISFRecordPortContexts` now prepares selected transaction set/update RHS,
when/while/until conditions, switch selectors/branches, nested bodies, rule
guards/assignments, named/inline drive bodies and named-drive actuals. Whole
record ports refuse scalar contexts, including negated and compact comparison
spellings. Port-involved whole assignments consume qualified recursive type
identity and role gates; input targets, bad paths, operator-position paths and
unsupported subaggregate uses refuse. Existing storage-only packed transfers
retain their original owner. Explicit leaf sampling, domain ownership and
first source admission remain separate prerequisites.

The gate validates references, not the complete source grammar. Unknown tokens,
operator/arity/static-value rules and enum/package member validation retain
their existing validators. State-active arguments denote states, and local/
parameter declaration names are not read operands. No successful preparatory
gate establishes that an otherwise invalid source is accepted.

A scalar pin may share an enum/package root name. Actual namespace roots remain
delegated unless the nearest aggregate or an explicitly shadowed outer
aggregate identifies a declaration path. The draft incorrectly rejected the
admitted enum token `mode.BUSY` when the actor had scalar input `mode`.
T1988 retains the repaired source control and the counterexample in which a
scalar formal must not borrow a same-named outer record's member via an enum.
Common aggregate/enum/rule root projection is prepared below; frontend integration remains pending.

## Qualification and limits

T1987's fresh copied actor/transaction/drive controls first reproduce the scalar
kind change; T1986's independently authored typed JSON does so for each value
gate. All preserve complete caller products after the repair. T1988 retains
independent selected AST cases and exact first-line negatives, same-type alias
copies, equal-width signed/state mismatches, input writes, formal shadows,
unknown-path controls, unsupported sampling/count/trigger contexts and enum
delegation. Complete currently admitted parser and scheduled products, including
emitted file bytes, remain unchanged. No oracle normalizes the caller product
before comparison.

```bash
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl \
  t/1988-isf-record-port-context-gates.t \
  t/1987-isf-record-port-declaration-scopes.t \
  t/1986-isf-record-port-value-gates.t \
  t/1983-isf-interface-port-metadata.t \
  t/1259-isf-aggregate-storage-type-aliases.t t/1391-isf-local-variables.t
```

The competing borrowed-type, whole-record scalar, equal-width identity and
post-read detachment interpretations fail independent witnesses and negative
controls. Producers and permanent source/AST controls are tracked; ignored
logs are supplementary. This establishes unwired preparation and the repaired
caller-data contract, not new source/public transport admission, sample timing,
generated/domain carriers, external HDL execution or complete consumer delivery.

## Common root-classification preparation

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.2.3` prepares `record_context_scope` and
`record_reference_root_kind` in the existing scope owner. One actual actor,
transaction or drive declaration selection supplies detached value roots,
resolved aggregate traversal roots, enum-exclusion roots, existing namespace
roots and actor rule-declaration roots. Transaction locals/formals and drive
parameters never become actor rule inputs. Rule roots also retain authored
storage signals, parameters/constants and legacy/named-domain clock/reset pins.

Nearest scalar or unresolved bindings remove an outer record from aggregate
traversal while keeping that outer name excluded from enum fallback. Scalar
pins that only share an enum/package root remain namespace tokens. Member
validity and enum/package resolution stay with their existing owners; root
classification does not turn an unknown member into a valid value.

The unwired contextual gate consumes this common projection instead of its
private namespace classifier. Existing frontend aggregate/enum/rule validators
remain unchanged until sampling/domain prerequisites permit source integration.
This is deliberate preparation, not record authoring or carrier admission.
T1989 independently expects every map and tests actual imported enum/type/
constant facts, named-domain system pins, nearest scalar/unresolved/drive shadows,
input roles, first-read caller JSON and separate output-map mutation isolation.
T1985 and T1982 qualify complete current public transport products and historical
domain reports, actual IAL0 carriers and generated HDL bytes except date. The
combined producer command and captured result are retained by this leaf in
the task evidence; no new authored record-port behavior is established.

## Explicit scalar-leaf sample facts

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.3.1` prepares `ISFRecordPortSamples` without source or
carrier wiring. Actual transaction scopes resolve explicit entry/body/control
sample sources into detached scalar references, root-relative ranges and local
alias bindings. A record leaf retains scalar kind, width, signed property and
optional state model; chained explicit samples retain their record provenance.
Unknown/formal/enum facts remain unknown or delegated, and an explicit sample
alias masks outer declaration facts without borrowing a record layout. No
implicit sample or declaration is inferred from unrelated assignments.

Whole records/subaggregates, invalid members/items, input targets, existing
declaration collisions for private record-derived aliases and inconsistent
repeated sample types refuse. Repeated explicit captures of the same scalar
type may reuse their own alias. A record-derived alias cannot replace authored
local/formal/storage/output declarations or inherit their reset/type metadata.

A separate pure type-product boundary generates ordinary core scalar type ASTs,
type references and exact widths only for record-derived aliases. Private type
names are sorted and deterministically reserve existing names before suffixing
collisions. Signed and declared two/four-state wrappers are retained; no backend
state default, reset/default fact or hardware edge is introduced. The actual
public type resolver reconstructs these scalar properties independently.

T1990 retains an independently authored nine-bit nested layout, exact scalar
facts, imported aliases, formal/local/unresolved and namespace shadows, repeated
captures, declaration/role/path negatives and complete first-read copied JSON
isolation. Its first lexical-local fixture failed because the helper replaced
all clauses, removing the declaration; the repaired control retains that actual
local AST. A separate draft collision predicate trusted a previous sample alias
and permitted scalar-then-record sample reuse of authored storage `held`. An
isolated copy of that predicate makes the permanent declaration-collision
witness RED. The production gate retains the original declaration set, so no
intermediate sample scope can erase an authored collision. Existing entry/
piggyback/pre-data capture and malformed-source tests remain green. Complete current parsed/scheduled products stay unchanged. Native
structured authored record-input refusal is also retained at this boundary.

The task leaf retains the combined producing command and captured result.
Permanent source/AST witnesses falsify width-only, outer-type borrowing, shared
output-map and leaked reset/default interpretations. Producers are tracked;
ignored logs are supplementary. Typed private carrier integration and actual
IAL0 replay/timing remain `.3.3.2` and `.3.3.3`; first authored record admission
and independently supervised HDL behavior retain their later owners.

## Contextual sample consumption

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.3.2.1` lets the unwired contextual gate consume the ordered
sample plan for supplied resolved record-input actors. Explicit entry/body/
control leaf samples receive local scalar alias bindings before contextual
reads/copies. Input roles, exact alias widths and scalar path refusals remain
qualified; sampling cannot replace an authored declaration or invent a record.

The consumer's `port_only` selection delegates existing storage-only aggregate
samples to their packed-width/inference owner; no new aggregate alias layout is
borrowed. Ordinary scalar, formal/local and namespace facts retain their existing
contracts. An unresolved forward sample chain which later names a record-derived
alias refuses rather than losing its newly resolved signed/state facts. Sample
collection does not reorder any capture state or permit a new clause placement.

T1991 covers entry, standalone, nested control and chained samples, independently

selected-sample controls RED: its first diagnostic refuses packet.count through
`_unsupported`. The new consumer passes without changing parser, scheduler or

Module widths/types, actual generated-helper/private alias ownership and full
replay/capture qualification remain the next children. The combined command and

producer and permanent AST controls retain re-derivation, falsification and

behavior or native HDL execution is established here.

## Selector shape validation precedes dereference

The `.3.3.2.1` draft selector read `type_spec` from an unchecked input entry.
A direct first-touch call returned false but changed caller `inputs` from

```bash
perl -MJSON::PP -e 'my $j=JSON::PP->new->canonical; my $a=[undef]; print $j->encode($a),"\n"; my $unused=$a->[0]{type_spec}; print $j->encode($a),"\n";'
```

`24d0abf84622ffaf6e665ae425e86f687968995c` makes these type/width/private-carrier

## Actual sample ownership and metadata first-touch repair

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.3.2.3` qualifies actual private sample ownership through

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.3.3` closes sampling preparation through T1994 at production

# SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER: Semantic Introspection And MCP Frontier

## Metadata

- Tree ID: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER`
- Status: `active`
- Roadmap lane: `Embedding And Public APIs / AI integration`
- Created: `2026-06-14`
- Last updated: `2026-10-03`
- Owner: repo-local workflow

## Goal

Make deep semantic introspection a first-class FSMGen feature: every meaningful
FSMGen semantic domain must become queryable through a clean, bounded API and
MCP must expose that API without leaking private implementation structures.

## Applied Direction From The RTL Simulator MCP Discussion

FSMGen can apply the same core principle: do not make the compiler/lowering
engine "MCP-first"; make it "stable semantic API first, MCP-exposed second."
For FSMGen, the analogs are:

- Simulator `compile/elaborate/run` maps to FSMGen `check`, `lower`, `emit
  semantic JSON`, `emit schedule JSON`, and `generate HDL`.
- Simulator hierarchy/driver/waveform queries map to FSMGen source identity,
  capability discovery, normalized semantic summaries, lowering-stage review
  artifacts, generated-artifact inventories, provenance, diagnostics, and
  support-accounting queries.
- Simulator waveform slices do not apply directly; FSMGen should expose
  structured semantic slices rather than large raw internal dumps.
- Simulator coverage-closure workflows map to FSMGen support-coverage and
  example-discovery workflows: find runnable examples, identify unsupported
  constructs, explain diagnostics, and select the nearest supported spelling.
- Simulator assertion/monitor generation maps to FSMGen verification-intent
  assistance: propose `.isf`/`.fsm` assertion or property forms, then let
  FSMGen check/generate exact diagnostics and HDL.
- Simulator regression triage maps to FSMGen corpus/check/semantic triage:
  classify parse, support-accounting, lowering, backend, and external
  validation failures.
- Simulator service API maps to a future long-lived or in-process FSMGen
  semantic service only if repeated fine-grained queries justify it. The first
  safe adapter may still drive existing stable CLI JSON surfaces.

## Existing Surfaces To Reuse

- `./bin/fsmgen --capability-manifest`
- `./bin/fsmgen --check --json`
- `./bin/fsmgen --emit-semantic-json`
- `./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json` for `.isf` / `.ppif` lowering review
- generated `.isf` / `.fsm` / HDL artifact reporting
- support accounting and stable diagnostic-code registry
- normalized semantic contracts under `perl/FSM/Support/NormalizedSemantic*`
- embedding-facing manifest contracts under `perl/FSM/Support/*Contract.pm`
- mdBook examples and checked-in corpus entries as user-facing examples

## Non-Goals

- Do not implement MCP, service APIs, new CLI commands, new generated
  artifacts, or behavior-bearing API changes without activating an exact leaf.
- Do not expose raw Perl AST objects, raw private scheduler/lowering objects,
  raw `LoweringIR`, or unstable whole-hash payloads as public API.
- Do not add arbitrary shell access, unrestricted file writes, network access,
  or unbounded workspace traversal through any future MCP adapter.
- Do not make MCP define the semantic contract for IAL0, IAL1, or IAL2; MCP
  exposes the bounded public semantic-introspection API.
- Do not continue broad IAL2 feature-completeness work ahead of this lane
  while an exact semantic-introspection leaf is the active priority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The first active selector inventories current machine-readable surfaces and
  selects a bounded semantic-introspection contract boundary before any
  implementation.
- Future implementation exposes MCP through the selected semantic API instead
  of through raw private compiler objects or ad hoc command text.
- Any future implementation leaf names exact resources, tools, prompts,
  schemas, safety policy, tests, docs, and rollback plan before source changes.
- Public docs and mdBook explain only shipped behavior; unshipped MCP adapter
  work stays clearly labeled as future until implemented.
- Each completed leaf is committed through `COMMIT.md`.

  Status: `active`
  Goal: `Track first-class semantic introspection and MCP query API work.`
  Children: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.1, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.2, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.3, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.4, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.5, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.6, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.7, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.8, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.9, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.10, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.11, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.12, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.13, SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.14,
